precepts.text: The men of Ephraim chided sharply with Gideon for not calling them to the battle against the Midianites; that war-like spirit was always in Ephraim.
precepts.point: Ephraim being greater goes into Ephraim becoming the head of the ten tribes, the head of the kingdom of Samaria; and it was Ephraim that led the charge, with the help of Issachar and Manasseh, that brought the ten tribes from the eastern hemisphere to the western hemisphere. The unicorn there is not a fairy tale horse; the original etymology goes into the rhinoceros.

note.label: Joshua 17: The Lot of Manasseh and the Blessing of Ephraim

precepts.why:
In Judges 7 Manasseh went to war with the three hundred men and destroyed the Midianites though they were lower in numbers, because Christ gave them the victory. Then in Judges 8: “And the men of Ephraim said unto him, Why hast thou served us thus, that thou calledst us not, when thou wentest to fight with the Midianites? And they did chide with him sharply.”

Ephraim was upset that they were not called to help in that war. That war-like spirit was always in Ephraim; they always had that leadership attribute, that military spirit, the vigorous leadership. It is the same spirit that drove out the Canaanites with their iron chariots, where Manasseh had issues.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

precepts.why:
Gideon said to Jether his firstborn, “Up, and slay them. But the youth drew not his sword: for he feared, because he was yet a youth.” We have all had that moment of getting the nudge from pops and being nervous; the son was young, and that is understandable. But look at Gideon being a father, taking his son to the war and teaching him the ways he must walk.

“Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.” Gideon is doing exactly what we have to do with our young men, teaching them how to walk in the ways of the Lord, even bringing them to the battle so they learn it.

precepts.text: The love of money is the root of all evil; the gold that Gideon gathered turned into the very snare that trapped his own house.
precepts.point: Gideon made an ephod thereof and put it in his city, even in Ophrah: and all Israel went thither a whoring after it, which thing became a snare unto Gideon, and to his house.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

precepts.why:
“For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.”

Gideon gathered “a thousand and seven hundred shekels of gold” in earrings, “beside ornaments, and collars, and purple raiment that was on the kings of Midian, and beside the chains that were about their camels’ necks.” He made an ephod of it and put it in Ophrah, “and all Israel went thither a whoring after it: which thing became a snare unto Gideon, and to his house.” The gold that Gideon gathered turned into the very snare that trapped his own house; he pierced himself through with many sorrows.

precepts.point: The sum of the history of Gideon, who is also named Jerubbaal, is this: the victory does not come in the strength of numbers, in how many guns or how many bullets you have. note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

precepts.why:
The sum of the history of Gideon, who is also named Jerubbaal, is that the victory does not come in the strength of numbers, in how many guns or how many bullets you have. Judas Maccabaeus learned the same lesson. He “went forth to meet him with a small company”, and his men asked, “How shall we be able, being so few, to fight against so great a multitude and so strong, seeing we are ready to faint with fasting all this day?”

Judas answered just as the history of Gideon teaches: “It is no hard matter for many to be shut up in the hands of a few; and with the God of heaven it is all one, to deliver with a great multitude, or a small company: For the victory of battle standeth not in the multitude of an host; but strength cometh from heaven.”

“They come against us in much pride and iniquity to destroy us, and our wives and children, and to spoil us: But we fight for our lives and our laws. Wherefore the Lord himself will overthrow them before our face: and as for you, be ye not afraid of them.” Midian was subdued before three hundred men “so that they lifted up their heads no more.” The victory of battle comes from the Lord, and that is why we have to trust in the Lord with all our heart and endure to the end, keeping these commandments until the return of our King of kings.

precepts.text: Midian was subdued and the country was in quietness forty years in the days of Gideon; Gideon had threescore and ten sons of his body begotten, for he had many wives, and his concubine that was in Shechem also bare him a son, whose name he called Abimelech.
precepts.point: Remember also that I am your bone and your flesh: he reminded them that he was family. When people do that, they want you to remember that blood is thicker than water, so you will back them whether or not it is right.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

precepts.why:
Chapter 8 gives the background. “Thus was Midian subdued before the children of Israel, so that they lifted up their heads no more. And the country was in quietness forty years in the days of Gideon.” Then, “Gideon had threescore and ten sons of his body begotten: for he had many wives. And his concubine that was in Shechem, she also bare him a son, whose name he called Abimelech.”

That is who Abimelech is: the son of the concubine in Shechem, not of the wives. That is why he goes to Shechem, “unto his mother’s brethren”, his uncles on his mother's side, and has them ask the men of Shechem whether all seventy sons should reign or one. And it is why he says, “remember also that I am your bone and your flesh.” He reminded them he was family. When people do that, they want you to remember that blood is thicker than water, so you will back them whether or not it is right.

precepts.text: After Gideon led the three hundred, the men of Israel said, Rule thou over us, both thou and thy son and thy son's son also, for thou hast delivered us from the hand of Midian.
precepts.point: So the Lord sent Jerubbaal, which is Gideon, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered Israel out of the hand of their enemies on every side, and they dwelled safe. None of those saviors had to wear a crown.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
After Gideon led the three hundred, “the men of Israel said unto Gideon, Rule thou over us, both thou, and thy son, and thy son’s son also: for thou hast delivered us from the hand of Midian.”

Gideon is Jerubbaal, one of the deliverers Samuel names: “the Lord sent Jerubbaal, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered you out of the hand of your enemies on every side, and ye dwelled safe.” This is the history of the book of Judges. When Israel forgat the Lord their God, he sold them into the hand of Sisera, of the Philistines, and of the king of Moab; when they cried, “We have sinned, because we have forsaken the Lord, and have served Baalim and Ashtaroth”, he sent a deliverer.

The people wanted to make their deliverer a king. But none of those saviors had to wear a crown.

precepts.text: Gideon refused: I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you; the Lord shall rule over you. He knew that if thrones were set up, the people would put their trust and faith in the king instead of the Most High; it was never the Lord's intention to set kings in the flesh over Israel, he was to be our king.
precepts.point: So the Lord sent Jerubbaal, which is Gideon, and Bedan, and Jephthah, and Samuel, and delivered Israel out of the hand of their enemies on every side, and they dwelled safe. None of those saviors had to wear a crown.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
“And Gideon said unto them, I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you: the Lord shall rule over you.”

Gideon refused. He knew that if thrones were set up, the people would put their trust and faith in the king instead of the Most High. It was never the Lord’s intention to set kings in the flesh over Israel; he was to be our king.

That is Samuel’s point in rehearsing the deliverers. Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah and Samuel delivered Israel on every side, and Israel dwelled safe, without a crown. What Israel needed was not a king but to put away the idols. It is not just about having the ark of the covenant among you, as when Israel went and got the ark against the Philistines, got beat even worse, and lost the ark. You have to put away the idols and stop serving Baalim and Ashtaroth.

points: The men of Ephraim chode with Gideon sharply: why hast thou served us thus, that thou calledst us not when thou wentest to fight with the Midianites? Ephraim has an attitude because they got called late to the battle and wanted in from the beginning.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Gideon answers with wisdom: is not the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer? God delivered into your hands the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; what was I able to do in comparison of you? He gave them the best possible situation, the enemy fed right into their hands with nowhere to go, and then their anger was abated toward him.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Gideon and the three hundred pass over Jordan, faint, yet pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna the kings of Midian. He asks the men of Succoth for loaves of bread for his men, and the princes of Succoth answer, are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in thine hand, that we should give bread unto thine army? They try to play neutral ground for fear the kings might come against them if they helped.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Gideon promises Succoth that when the Lord has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into his hand, he will tear their flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers; and when the men of Penuel answer him the same way, he promises to break down their tower when he comes again in peace.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with about fifteen thousand men, all that were left of the host of the children of the east, for there fell an hundred and twenty thousand men that drew sword. Three hundred against those numbers: you know God was with them.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Gideon went up by the way of them that dwelt in tents and smote the host while it was secure, and when the two kings fled, he pursued and took them, and discomfited all the host.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: Returning from battle, Gideon caught a young man of Succoth who described unto him the princes and elders of the city, and he came back to Succoth with Zebah and Zalmunna in hand: behold the kings with whom ye did upbraid me. Gideon and his men had finished off Midian on an empty stomach because of them.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal

points: He took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth; he taught them a lesson, that when the army of the Lord comes through faint and weary and asks for bread, you do not turn them away. And he beat down the tower of Penuel and slew the men of the city.

note.label: Judges 8: Gideon's Pursuit and Israel's Return to Baal
